text: Two features with genuinely similar names, and two genuinely different jobs. Let's tell them apart clearly, because mixing these up is one of the more common points of confusion in Power BI reporting.

Drill mode stays entirely inside one visual — up a level, down a level, or expand every level at once, the same four icons you already saw back in Chapter 7's third lesson on core charts. It's a way of moving through a hierarchy without ever leaving the chart you started on.

Drillthrough is bigger than that: it actually takes you to an entirely separate report page. Add a new page, expand the Drillthrough section in the Visualizations pane, and drag a field into the Drillthrough filters well — Power BI adds a Back button to that page automatically. Build the visuals on it around that one filtered item specifically — a card showing its name, a table of its history, a trend line over time — rather than reusing whatever sat on the summary page.

Right-click any data point that shares the drillthrough field, hover over Drillthrough in the context menu, and pick the target page — Power BI navigates there instantly, already filtered to exactly what you clicked. A button with its action set to Drillthrough does the same job, just visibly, for viewers who'd never think to right-click. Drillthrough can even jump between two entirely separate reports, once cross-report drillthrough is enabled in the target's settings.
Next: buttons, bookmarks, and navigation — building a genuinely guided report experience instead of a single static page a viewer has to figure out alone.
